newsitem.title: USA: United American halts Pa., Ga. initiatives.
newsitem.headline: United American halts Pa., Ga. initiatives.

text.p: United American Healthcare Corp said it is withdrawing its support of PhilCare Health System Inc's application to participate in the Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare HealthChoices program, a proposed Medicaid managed care initiative.

PhilCare is a health maintenance organization, or HMO, that is 49-percent owned by United American. "After prolonged negotiations with the commonwealth of Pennsylvania, we feel it is in the best interest of our shareholders to withdraw from consideration in the HealthChoices program," said United American chief executive Julius Combs.
The Detroit-based company also said it is dropping its licensing application in Georgia.

"We are making a serious effort to review our growth strategy and evaluate the potential benefit to shareholders in each of our markets. The cessation of our initiatives in both Pennsylvania and Georgia is the direct result of this intensified focus," Combs said.

United American manages four HMOs under long-term contracts. The company, through Baltimore-based Corporate Healthcare Financing, also provides management and advisory services to companies that self-fund their benefit plans.
United American also operates a preferred provider network under the name ChoiceOne.
Shares in United American were off 1/8 to 6-1/8.
